## Overview

Datasets describe field experiments where a soil carbon or greenhouse gas response was measured against a control, so a model can be tested on two things at once: absolute value, and treatment difference (practice change signal that policy applications care about).

**Key features:**

- **Model agnostic.** Observations stay in reported units with no model specific transformation. Mapping to model state variables happens downstream.
- **Long format observations**, one row per dataset, site, treatment, replicate, time window, and variable, at replicate level where source archive provides it.
- **Stable text keys** (`dataset_id`, `site`, `treatment_id`, `citation`) rather than database identifiers.
- **Per row provenance** through `fill_status`, recording which source file each value came from.
- **Source stated date ranges** in `min_date` and `max_date`; point dates are never invented.
- **Named treatment contrasts** in `treatment_pairs`, so practice change validation (compost vs no compost, cover crop vs none, organic vs conventional) is a first class query.
- **Coverage matrix** tracking which system, contrast, and target cells are filled, so gaps stay explicit.

The statewide synthesis evidence is kept apart from these tables, in [`data_raw/statewide_benchmarking/`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/tree/develop/data_raw/statewide_benchmarking). Its [README](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/data_raw/statewide_benchmarking/README.md) describes the files, and [Part B](../reports/statewide-evidence.qmd) of the report describes the evidence.

## Data flow

Curation happens in Google Sheet workbooks, which are the source of truth. CSVs in `data/` and `data_raw/statewide_benchmarking/` are generated exports and must not be hand edited.

1. The workbooks hold the curated tables and are edited and reviewed there. [`000-config.yml`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/000-config.yml) lists the three dataset workbooks: Salinas and Modesto, Russell Ranch, and the AmeriFlux Delta towers.
2. [`scripts/ingest.R`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/scripts/ingest.R) pulls each workbook tab to `data/<tab>.csv`, stacking the tab across all three workbooks.
3. [`scripts/validate.R`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/scripts/validate.R) checks `data/` against [`datapackage.json`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/datapackage.json).
4. [`scripts/ingest_benchmarking.R`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/scripts/ingest_benchmarking.R) pulls the synthesis and meta-analysis evidence workbook into [`data_raw/statewide_benchmarking/`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/tree/develop/data_raw/statewide_benchmarking), one CSV per worksheet except its README. With `--check` it compares the workbook with the committed CSVs and writes nothing.
5. Downstream consumers read committed CSVs.

CSVs are committed so consumers read a stable, documented snapshot. A workbook can keep changing without a commit per edit; CSVs are regenerated and committed when a dataset version is ready.

## Datasets

Each site level dataset has a folder under [`data_raw/`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/tree/develop/data_raw) whose `data_entry_report.md` records its provenance and curation decisions. Replicate level values come from a public archive wherever one provides them; companion analysis papers supply methods and cross checks. Each dataset group is curated in its own workbook, and ingest stacks each tab across all workbooks into one CSV per table.

| dataset_id | site | lat, lon | period | treatments | variables | citations (DOI) |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |

: Curated site level datasets. {#tbl-datasets}

The annual NEE and tower CH~4~ rows at the three Delta sites, and the annual chamber rows taken from publication tables at the two Bouldin sites, carry the upstream product or publication as their `dataset_id`, for example `ameriflux_fluxnet_1f_us_bi1_v1_3_r1`, `fluxnet_ch4_community_product_v1_appendix_b_v2` or `publication_anthony_2023_table_1`. `data/observations.csv` therefore holds 14 `dataset_id` values in all.

### white_salinas_2020

Organic vegetable rotation (romaine lettuce, broccoli) with winter cover crops and compost. Randomized complete block, 4 blocks, so block level is replicate level here. Companion analysis paper focuses on 5 systems (those with optimal cover crop seeding rates); workbook carries all 8 from archive. SOC stock is concentration times bulk density times depth (0 to 30 cm), with bulk density measured only at end of Years 3 and 7 and propagated by equivalent soil mass, so `core_sample` method row carries that propagation rule. A large Year 0 to Year 1 SOC drop appears across all systems including no compost control, and is documented in source.

### nichols_modesto_2024

Long term compost orchard with high frequency low concentration drip fertigation (about 195 kg N ha^-1^ across 14 events). N~2~O measured by closed static chamber on 9 dates (Dec 2018 to Aug 2019), 3 replicate arrays per treatment, upscaled to emitter level. Soil total C, total N, and bulk density are single timepoint (August 2019), so this dataset supports N~2~O magnitude and contrast validation but not a SOC trajectory.

## Measured variables

Core variables, in reported units:

| variable | units | description |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SOC_stock_Mg_ha` | Mg C ha^-1^ | soil organic carbon stock; `min_depth` / `max_depth` give the sampled interval for fixed-depth stocks and the reference interval for equivalent-soil-mass stocks |
| `SOC_conc_mg_kg` | mg C kg^-1^ soil | soil organic carbon concentration |
| `bulk_density_g_cm3` | g cm^-3^ | soil bulk density |
| `total_N_conc_mg_kg` | mg N kg^-1^ soil | total soil nitrogen concentration |
| `nitrate_N_mg_kg` | mg NO~3~-N kg^-1^ soil | soil nitrate nitrogen |
| `N2O_flux_g_N_ha_d` | g N~2~O-N ha^-1^ day^-1^ | nitrous oxide flux |
| `total_C_pct` | % dry weight | total soil carbon by dry combustion |
| `total_N_pct` | % dry weight | total soil nitrogen by dry combustion |

: Core measured variables. {#tbl-core-variables}

The Delta tower and Bouldin chamber datasets add the gas flux variables below. The units column is as [`data/variables.csv`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/data/variables.csv) gives it; each row keeps the source's own units in `reported_units`.

| variable | units | reported units | measurement support | rows |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---: |
| `N2O_flux_mg_m2_d` | mg N~2~O m^-2^ d^-1^ | mg N~2~O m^-2^ d^-1^ | automated chamber, US-Bi1 and US-Bi2 (`anthony_bouldin_2024`) | 70 |
| `CH4_flux_mg_m2_d` | mg CH~4~ m^-2^ d^-1^ | mg CH~4~ m^-2^ d^-1^ | automated chamber, US-Bi1 and US-Bi2 (`anthony_bouldin_2024`) | 70 |
| `CO2_flux_g_m2_d` | g CO~2~ m^-2^ d^-1^ | g CO~2~ m^-2^ d^-1^ | opaque automated chamber, respiration only, US-Bi1 and US-Bi2 (`anthony_bouldin_2024`) | 70 |
| `CH4_flux` | kg C m^-2^ s^-1^ (daily mean); kg C m^-2^ year^-1^ (annual total) | g C m^-2^ yr^-1^ (11 rows); mg CH~4~ m^-2^ yr^-1^ (4); mg CH~4~ m^-2^ y^-1^ (3) | eddy covariance annual totals at US-Twt, US-Bi1 and US-Bi2 (11 rows); automated chamber annual means from publication tables at the US-Bi1 alfalfa chambers and US-Bi2 (7 rows) | 18 |
| `N2O_flux` | source-reported units | mg N~2~O m^-2^ yr^-1^ (4); g N~2~O m^-2^ y^-1^ (3) | automated chamber annual means from publication tables, US-Bi1 alfalfa chambers and US-Bi2 | 7 |
| `NEE` | kg C m^-2^ s^-1^ (daily mean); kg C m^-2^ year^-1^ (annual total) | gC m^-2^ y^-1^ | eddy covariance annual totals, US-Bi1 (8), US-Bi2 (7), US-Twt (6) | 21 |

: Gas flux variables of the Delta tower and Bouldin chamber datasets. {#tbl-flux-variables}

`CH4_flux` holds both tower and chamber values, told apart by the `method` column. Chamber and tower values are different measurement supports and are not interchangeable.

Supporting variables (soil organic matter fractions, texture, pH, biomass, yields, nitrogen inputs) accompany core targets where source reports them. The full list of 104 variables lives in [`data/variables.csv`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/data/variables.csv).

## Coverage

[`data/coverage.csv`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/data/coverage.csv) crosses system and treatment contrast against each target, split into magnitude and treatment contrast, for SOC change, N~2~O, CH~4~ and woody biomass. Target cells are coded 1 where current datasets cover them and 0 where they are tracked gaps. The planning matrix, with the SOC change and N~2~O columns and 1 shown as yes:

| System | Treatment contrast | ΔSOC magnitude | ΔSOC contrast | N~2~O magnitude | N~2~O contrast | source |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | :------------: | :-----------: | :-------------: | :------------: | ------------------------------------------- |
| Annual row / vegetable | cover crop vs no cover crop | yes | yes |  |  | white_salinas_2020 |
| Annual row / vegetable | compost / OM vs fertilizer | yes | yes |  |  | white_salinas_2020 (N~2~O not measured) |
| Perennial woody (orchard / vineyard) | one management contrast with known history |  |  | yes | yes | nichols_modesto_2024 (single timepoint SOC) |
| Annual or perennial | tillage contrast |  |  |  |  | gap |
| Annual or perennial | irrigation regime contrast |  |  |  |  | gap |
| Rice / flooded | flood vs AWD |  |  |  |  | gap |

: Planning matrix of system and treatment contrast against SOC change and N~2~O targets. {#tbl-coverage}

The matrix predates the Russell Ranch, AmeriFlux Delta and Bouldin chamber datasets. Russell Ranch adds SOC change magnitude and contrasts on annual row crops, among them cover cropping, compost against synthetic fertiliser, rotation and irrigation ([A7](../reports/site-level-data.qmd#a7-practice-contrasts)). **N~2~O is covered at three sites** (`nichols_modesto_2024` static chamber; `anthony_bouldin_2024` automated chamber at US-Bi2 and US-Bi1) and **CH~4~ at three** (tower annual budgets for US-Twt, US-Bi1 and US-Bi2, plus chamber CH~4~ at the two Bouldin sites). Chamber and tower values are different measurement supports and are not interchangeable. [A4](../reports/site-level-data.qmd#a4-what-is-measured-and-where) in the report shows the target records by site and variable.

Because ingest stacks the coverage tab from every workbook, the file holds the matrix and its MVP coverage guidance twice, the second copy with every SOC, N~2~O and CH~4~ cell 0, followed by six rows of record counts for `CH4_flux` and `NEE` at US-Bi1, US-Bi2 and US-Twt.

## Data products

Each workbook tab maps to one CSV in `data/`. Full field schema, types, and keys live in [datapackage.json](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/datapackage.json); two core tables are described below.

### Table inventory

| CSV | Purpose | Key |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `citations.csv` | bibliographic sources | `citation_id` |
| `sites.csv` | site name and coordinates | `name` |
| `treatments.csv` | treatment and system definitions, control flag | `name` |
| `treatment_pairs.csv` | named contrasts for treatment difference validation | `pair_id` |
| `managements.csv` | agronomic events (planting, harvest, tillage, fertilization, amendment) | `event_id` |
| `observations.csv` | measured data, long format | none declared |
| `methods.csv` | how each measurement was taken | `method name` |
| `variables.csv` | variable dictionary (name, description, units) | `name` |
| `crops.csv` | crop and cover crop species | `scientific name` |
| `coverage.csv` | coverage planning matrix | |

: Tables in data/. {#tbl-inventory}

In `observations.csv` and `managements.csv`, `citation` holds a DOI and refers to `citations.doi`, while `citation_id` refers to `citations.citation_id`.

### observations.csv columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| ------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `min_date`, `max_date` | string | source stated window; equal for a point sample, blank when source gives no date; date encodings are mixed in the current export |
| `crop`, `variety` | string | crop and variety, where reported |
| `sitename` | string | foreign key to `sites.name` |
| `variable` | string | foreign key to `variables.name` |
| `method` | string | measurement method (see `methods.csv`) |

| `n` | number | sample size; 1 for replicate level rows |
| `statname`, `stat` | string, number | reported statistic (e.g. SE) and its value; not converted during curation |
| `treatment_id` | string | foreign key to `treatments.name` |
| `replicate_id` | string | block, plot, core, or chamber identifier as the source uses it; numeric at some sites, lettered blocks or named zones at others |

| `min_depth`, `max_depth` | number | cm; sampled interval for depth-based observations and reference interval for equivalent-soil-mass stocks; actual integrated depth is recorded in `attributes_json.equivalent_depth_cm` |

| `fill_status` | string | provenance code (see [Conventions](#conventions)) |
| `notes` | string | free text, including date precision caveats |

| `reported_units` | string | units as source reports them |
| `observation_level` | string | experimental unit the row represents: `replicate`, `treatment_mean`, `zone_mean`, `site_layer`, `site_year_total` or `site_period_total` |
| `citation_id` | string | citation this observation was drawn from; refers to `citations.citation_id`, not a DOI |
| `data_origin` | string | how the value was obtained, e.g. publication_table, publication_text, scripted aggregation |

Smaller tables (`citations`, `sites`, `treatments`, `treatment_pairs`, `methods`, `variables`, `crops`) are short; see [datapackage.json](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/datapackage.json) for their fields.

## Conventions

- **Stable text keys.** A site key is physical location only; it does not encode treatment, replicate, or date. Treatment keys (`socs_sys1`, `compost`, `no_compost`) stay stable across a dataset.
- **Long format, replicate level.** Where a paper has a companion data archive, ingest replicate level values from archive; summary tables in analysis paper are for cross checking, not primary fill source.
- **Dates.** Record source stated range in `min_date` and `max_date`. An exact date sets both equal; a stated month or season bounds interval; an unknown date stays blank with reason in `notes`. Never invent a day of year.
- **Statistics.** Store reported statistic (`n`, `statname`, `stat`) as given. Statistic conversion (standard deviation to standard error, and similar) is a downstream step, not curation.
- **Basis.** Methods state dry vs wet basis (prefer dry) and volumetric vs mass basis. Amendment rates carry their basis in `units`.
- **fill_status.** Provenance code for each value. Codes in current data: FILLED_DATA_PUBLICATION, SCRIPTED_DERIVED, FILLED_ZOTERO_XLSX, FILLED_DATASET, FILLED_SITE_DATA_XLSX, REPORTED_DIRECT, FILLED_PUBLICATION_TABLE and FILLED_PUBLICATION_TEXT. `datapackage.json` also allows FILLED_S1_TABLE and FILLED_USDA_SOIL_XLSX. Additional codes (PAPER_TEXT, NEEDS_FILL, MISSING_IN_SOURCE) are reserved for rows still being curated.

## Validation

[`scripts/validate.R`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/scripts/validate.R) checks every generated `data/*.csv` against `datapackage.json`. It runs in warn mode: missing columns, empty keys, broken foreign keys, and odd dates warn but do not stop, so a workbook in progress still passes. It needs only base R plus `jsonlite` and `readr`.

```bash
Rscript scripts/validate.R
```

Tests under [`tests/testthat/`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/tree/develop/tests/testthat) run the same checks via testthat, plus checks on the statewide evidence; they also need `testthat` and `here`. Tables not yet generated are skipped, so a fresh clone passes.

```bash
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
```

CI ([`.github/workflows/validate.yml`](https://github.com/ccmmf/cal-val-data/blob/develop/.github/workflows/validate.yml)) runs both, plus `frictionless validate datapackage.json`, on every pull request and on pushes to `main`.

## Usage

### Load a table

```r
library(readr)
obs <- read_csv("data/observations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# replicate level SOC stock
subset(obs, variable == "SOC_stock_Mg_ha" & observation_level == "replicate")
```

### Pull a treatment contrast

```r
pairs <- read_csv("data/treatment_pairs.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# contrasts flagged for validation (e.g. compost vs no compost)
subset(pairs, use_for_validation == TRUE)
```

### Regenerate the snapshot from the workbooks

```r
# the workbook ids are in 000-config.yml; authenticate once
# interactively with googlesheets4::gs4_auth(), then
source("scripts/ingest.R")
```

The statewide evidence has its own script. Set `CCMMF_SHEETS_EMAIL` to the Google account that can read the evidence workbook.

```bash
Rscript scripts/ingest_benchmarking.R --check   # compare the workbook with the committed CSVs
Rscript scripts/ingest_benchmarking.R           # regenerate them
```

## Changes from the README {#changes-from-the-readme}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What was updated on 2026-09-30, against develop 900ffd2"}
- **Data flow.** Three dataset workbooks and a separate evidence workbook, where the README described one workbook; the evidence ingest is now its own numbered step.
- **Datasets.** Added the three AmeriFlux tower datasets, the upstream `dataset_id` values their flux rows carry, and a pointer to the statewide evidence folder.
- **Measured variables.** Added the gas flux variables of the Delta tower and Bouldin chamber datasets.
- **Coverage.** Target cells in the file are coded 1 and 0; the matrix also predates Russell Ranch; the stacked copies in the file are described.
- **Repository structure.** The tree showed an early layout; it now shows the current one, including the site files.
- **Table inventory.** `citations.csv` is keyed by `citation_id`, not `doi`, and `observations.csv` declares no primary key.
- **Column tables.** All 27 `observations.csv` and 26 `managements.csv` columns are listed, with the types `datapackage.json` declares (`replicate_id`, `min_date` and `max_date` are strings) and the allowed `observation_level` and `mgmttype` values.
- **Conventions.** The eight `fill_status` codes now in use, where the README listed three.
- **Validation and usage.** The statewide evidence tests, CI, and `scripts/ingest_benchmarking.R`.
:::
